parole.significato: A low, flat mass of floating ice.
parole.testo: Early 19th century. Probably from Norwegian Nynorsk flo (“layer, slab”), from Old Norse fló (“layer”).

parole.significato: The waste left at the end of the whaling process.
parole.testo: Early 20th century. From Norwegian Nynorsk grakse (“residue from the production of fish or whale oil”), from Norwegian Nynorsk dragse (“residue”), from Old Norse dregg. Doublet of dreg.

parole.significato: To bend or twist; wriggle back and forth.
parole.testo: From a merger of wangle, and dialectal Norwegian Nynorsk vingla (“to flutter, stumble about, go hither and thither, go astray, dangle”), related to Norwegian Bokmål vingle (“to wobble”), Swedish vingla (“to wobble”).

parole.significato: shining, shimmering; bright or flashing (of the sky after rain, particularly in summer)
parole.testo: Related to Scots glisk (“to glance, glimpse; to give a transient gleam”), and Shetlandic dialect of English glisk (“gleam of sunlight through cloud; a glow of heat from a fire”).
